anomalies.obs: The UART3 debug nets are attached to the MCU VCAP pins: on FCC1 the pins named VCAP (48, 73) carry UART3_TX_FCC/UART3_RX_FCC, and on NAVC1 the pins named VCAP_1/VCAP_2 (46, 47) carry UART3_TX_NAVC/UART3_RX_NAVC, which are the same nets driven by the CH330 debug bridge U12 on the Connections sheet. No decoupling capacitor is drawn on any VCAP pin of either MCU.
anomalies.exp: VCAP is the internal-regulator output of the STM32H7/STM32F4 and must be tied to ground through its required decoupling capacitor, not to signal lines; the USART3/UART3 debug lines belong on normal GPIO pins (the sheet notes even state 'USART3 Bootloader PC10/PC11' for the F4). The spec describes the debug path as UART-to-USB via the CH330 bridges, implying working UART pins.

evidence.quote: FCC sheet: pin '48' with net 'UART3_TX_FCC' beside symbol text 'VCAP'; pin '73' with 'UART3_RX_FCC' beside 'VCAP'
NAVC sheet: pins '46 UART3_TX_NAVC' / '47 UART3_RX_NAVC' beside 'VCAP_1'/'VCAP_2'; note 'USART3 Bootloader PC10/PC11'

anomalies.impact: The MCU core-supply decoupling (VCAP) is missing and shorted to UART nets, so both MCUs may fail to regulate/start, and the NAVC debug UART is connected to the wrong pins, breaking UART-to-USB debug.

parsed.summary: The power, I2C, SPI and sensor sections match the specification (including the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap), but the MCU VCAP pins are wired to the UART3 nets with no decoupling capacitors, which deviates from the intended design and would break the MCUs' internal supply and the debug link.
